title: 2nd Matter The Criterion Of Scientific Consensus

questions.question: What main rule is stated about people speaking on a topic in science or art?
questions.answer: Only those trained in that field can speak with real authority; outsiders cannot give final judgments in it.

questions.question: How does the example of the engineer and the physician support that rule?
questions.answer: It shows that being highly skilled in one field does not make a person reliable in a different field.

questions.question: Why are some philosophers described as especially unfit to judge spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because they are focused only on physical things and are cut off from deeper spiritual realities.

questions.question: In the passage, what kind of people are presented as united on sacred matters and belief in Divine oneness?
questions.answer: The People of Truth, especially spiritually advanced believers and saints, are presented as being in full agreement.

questions.question: What does the mention of Shaykh Gilani emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes deep spiritual experience, long discipline, and strong certainty in the truths of faith.

questions.question: How are the objections of material-focused philosophers compared to the testimony of spiritually knowledgeable people?
questions.answer: Their objections are shown as weak and insignificant compared with the powerful agreement of the spiritually grounded.

questions.question: What contrast is made between attention to the material world and understanding spiritual truth?
questions.answer: Getting lost in material details can make a person less able to grasp non-material truths.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do the denials of such philosophers carry little weight?
questions.answer: Because they speak outside their proper area and lack the spiritual insight needed for those questions.

questions.question: What overall message does the passage give about whom to trust in matters of faith?
questions.answer: Matters of faith should be learned from those with spiritual knowledge and proven experience, not from people limited to material thinking.

questions.question: What effect does the final image of weak sound versus powerful sound create?
questions.answer: It highlights how small and powerless those denials are beside the strong witness of the righteous.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the Second Matter?
questions.answer: Expertise is limited to its own field, so outsiders should not be treated as final authorities.

questions.question: Why can even a very accomplished person be unreliable outside his own specialty?
questions.answer: Because skill and learning do not automatically transfer from one subject to another.

questions.question: What point is made by comparing a famous engineer with even a very ordinary doctor?
questions.answer: In medical matters, the doctor’s judgment counts more than the engineer’s, even if the engineer is greater in his own field.

questions.question: What problem is identified in philosophers who are absorbed in the physical world?
questions.answer: Their thinking becomes restricted to what can be sensed, which makes them poor judges of spiritual realities.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s understanding, according to the passage, when he becomes distant from the spiritual side of life?
questions.answer: His perception becomes duller and less able to receive higher truths.

questions.question: Who are described as giving strong witness on sacred and spiritual truths?
questions.answer: A vast number of truthful and spiritually realized believers are described that way.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It shows that spiritual truths are not based on one person’s opinion but on broad and consistent testimony.

questions.question: What role does Shaykh Gilani play in the discussion?
questions.answer: He is given as an example of someone with high spiritual rank and deep certainty in matters of belief.

questions.question: How does the passage describe philosophers who are buried in tiny details of the physical world?
questions.answer: It portrays them as confused and overwhelmed, not as sound judges of Divine matters.

questions.question: What conclusion should the reader draw about objections raised against spiritual truths by such philosophers?
questions.answer: Those objections should not be treated as decisive because they lack the proper foundation.

questions.question: According to the passage, who cannot be part of true scholarly agreement in a field?
questions.answer: People who stand outside that field cannot be counted in its learned consensus.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress this point before discussing spiritual matters?
questions.answer: It prepares the reader to see that materialist thinkers are not qualified to rule on questions of faith.

questions.question: What is the lesson of the medical example?
questions.answer: Knowledge must be judged by relevance, not just by fame or intelligence.

questions.question: How are philosophers centered on matter portrayed?
questions.answer: They are shown as people whose minds are tied to the visible world and unable to rise to the unseen.

questions.question: What kind of subjects are said to lie beyond the reach of such thinkers?
questions.answer: Sacred, spiritual, and God-centered subjects are said to lie beyond their reach.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the agreement of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: It says they have full harmony on sacred matters and the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Why is long spiritual striving mentioned in connection with Shaykh Gilani?
questions.answer: To show that certainty in faith comes through serious inner work and spiritual growth.

questions.question: What three levels of certainty are mentioned in relation to him, and what do they suggest?
questions.answer: They suggest a complete and deep realization of belief from multiple degrees of certainty.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate the denials of philosophers when set against the witness of the righteous?
questions.answer: It treats those denials as too weak to stand against such massive spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What major comprehension point about authority is taught in this passage?
questions.answer: Real authority depends on proper knowledge and experience in the subject being discussed.

questions.question: What principle about judgment and expertise opens the passage?
questions.answer: A person should not be accepted as a final judge in a field he does not belong to.

questions.question: How does this principle challenge blind admiration of famous thinkers?
questions.answer: It reminds readers that greatness in one area does not mean greatness in every area.

questions.question: Why is a philosopher limited to what he can sense presented as unreliable in spiritual issues?
questions.answer: Because spiritual issues go beyond what the eyes and physical senses can measure.

questions.question: What moral or spiritual decline is linked to this type of philosopher?
questions.answer: He is described as becoming rougher and less responsive to spiritual light.

questions.question: What kind of community is described as standing together on truths about Allah and sacred realities?
questions.answer: A large body of truthful, spiritually awakened believers is described as standing together.

questions.question: Why is this united witness stronger than the objections of philosophers?
questions.answer: Because it comes from many qualified people with direct spiritual insight rather than from outsiders to the subject.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between spiritual discipline and certainty?
questions.answer: It suggests that steady spiritual effort leads to stronger and clearer certainty.

questions.question: Why does the passage include an honored saint as an example?
questions.answer: To give a concrete picture of someone whose life shows deep spiritual authority.

questions.question: What feeling does the final comparison create about philosophical denial?
questions.answer: It makes that denial seem tiny, weak, and unable to compete with the force of truth.

questions.question: Summarize the passage’s warning in one sentence.
questions.answer: Do not let people who are strangers to spiritual knowledge overrule those who truly know that path.

questions.question: What does the passage say about speaking decisively in matters of a specialized field?
questions.answer: Decisive speech belongs to those within that discipline, not to outsiders.

questions.question: How does the example of medicine and engineering make the point easy to understand?
questions.answer: It shows that even a top expert in one profession is not automatically an authority in another.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is criticized here?
questions.answer: A philosopher who is trapped in material concerns and cut off from spiritual understanding is criticized.

questions.question: Why are his denials considered unimportant in non-material matters?
questions.answer: Because he lacks the tools and insight needed to judge those matters properly.

questions.question: On what subjects do the People of Truth have full agreement?
questions.answer: They agree on sacred realities and on the unity of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the value of spiritual experience?
questions.answer: It implies that spiritual experience gives real weight and credibility in questions of faith.

questions.question: What does the long life of spiritual striving attributed to Shaykh Gilani help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that his testimony came from deep practice and mature certainty.

questions.question: Why does the passage contrast broad spiritual insight with attention to tiny material details?
questions.answer: To show that obsession with the small physical world can block a person from seeing greater truths.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the final comparison between a small insect sound and thunder?
questions.answer: It is meant to show the huge difference in strength between weak denial and powerful truth.

questions.question: If a student applied this lesson today, what wise approach would the passage support?
questions.answer: The student should seek guidance on faith from trustworthy scholars and spiritually grounded believers, not from voices limited to material assumptions.

questions.question: What standard for accepting a judgment is given at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: A judgment should be accepted as final only from those qualified in that exact subject.

questions.question: Why does the passage say outsiders cannot join the consensus of a field?
questions.answer: Because consensus depends on recognized knowledge within the discipline itself.

questions.question: What does the comparison between two professions teach about authority?
questions.answer: Authority comes from relevant expertise, not from general prestige.

questions.question: How are some philosophers shown to be narrowed in their outlook?
questions.answer: They are shown as limiting truth to the material world and visible things.

questions.question: What effect does that narrow outlook have on their ability to judge spiritual realities?
questions.answer: It makes their judgment weak and unreliable in those realities.

questions.question: Who are presented as the trustworthy witnesses in matters about Allah and the unseen?
questions.answer: The trustworthy witnesses are the many truthful people of spiritual knowledge and realization.

questions.question: Why is their agreement especially powerful in the argument?
questions.answer: Because a large number of qualified witnesses agreeing together gives strong support to the truth they affirm.

questions.question: What qualities of Shaykh Gilani are highlighted?
questions.answer: His spiritual vision, long years of devoted effort, and deep certainty are highlighted.

questions.question: How should the reader understand the passage’s question about the worth of philosophers’ objections?
questions.answer: The reader should understand that those objections are being dismissed as insignificant next to true spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What is the best one-sentence summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: In spiritual matters, the united witness of people grounded in truth outweighs the denial of thinkers confined to the material world.
